(Original review) My first visit was for composite resin veneers on my front teeth.
Initially, there were problems with food getting stuck around the veneers and the fillings were spaced unevenly, resulting in an unsightly appearance. The clinic scheduled a follow-up appointment. The same dentist meticulously corrected my front teeth, producing a much better and more aesthetically pleasing result that I found satisfactory.

Therefore, I decided to also have dentures made at the clinic to support them.

During the impression taking process, the clinic's technical staff member was a woman with dark skin, wearing a headscarf, and appeared to be middle-aged. She instructed me to bite on a molding tool made of what appeared to be wax or some other material. I felt pain in my mouth when I bit down. It might have been due to soreness from having had dental work done twice before, which we're not sure of. Before making the impressions, we informed the female dentist who examined us that we had recently had work done by a male dentist. The male dentist had warned us not to bite anything because our original tooth tissue was very thin. However, the technician still made us bite hard, saying it might hurt the bone. At that time, we were in pain throughout our gums and mouth.

Finally, something suspicious happened: after brushing our teeth at home, we felt that the corrected tooth protruded forward more than it should.

The clinic then called us in for a follow-up examination. During the examination room, we encountered the technician in question. There was no other doctor in the room, just Ms. Dear and that technician.

This technician became irritable and angry because we suspected the problem was due to the dental impressions. The technician spoke very rudely to us, even telling us to go to another clinic we preferred. This happened several times, including when they suggested we take our money and remove the dental equipment. Their behavior and language were unacceptable. Therefore, we responded with words of caution, reminding them that we are customers and have paid every penny. We didn't intend to get a refund; we were simply curious and wanted the dentist to examine the patient and listen to our concerns. This led to Ms. Dear intervening to calm the situation. Ms. Dear informed us that she would report the matter to management and that disciplinary action would be taken against the technician. We insisted that the technician call to apologize in person. Ultimately, Ms. Dear from the clinic called to apologize on behalf of the technician, stating that management had suspended him and would refund all the payment for the denture appointment. The clinic explained that they currently lacked a technician to oversee the dental procedure. We believed this explanation and did not pursue the matter further, considering it a charitable act and not wanting to tarnish the organization's reputation because of one individual.

However, we want everyone reading this to take this as a cautionary tale regarding encountering this particular technician. This individual is definitely unsuitable for this profession. The person in the news is considered highly emotionally dangerous.

If you encounter an unsuspecting customer, be wary of someone behaving in such a rude manner. We don't know how other clients of the clinic will spread the word or what their complaints will be.

However, we commend the management for resolving the issue and hope that our case will serve as an example to prevent similar problems from occurring in the future. The Thai proverb, "One rotten fish spoils the whole pond," applies in every era. Reputation isn't built easily, but it can be easily destroyed by one person, especially in a service industry like this, which relies on clients willing to pay for quality treatment.
